patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

Secondary_Symptoms: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands
Swelling and erythema of the left wrist
Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies trauma to the wrist, reports a history of knee pain that resolved on its own. No other systemic symptoms mentioned.

questions: Did the wrist pain start after a specific injury or fall, and if so, when did it occur?
“Is the wrist pain associated with visible swelling, redness, or warmth (either currently or at flare-ups)?”
Do you currently have (or have you ever had) fever, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss?
Have you had any swelling, visible lumps, or limited range of motion in the left wrist during the pain episodes?
During these episodes, do you have any urinary symptoms (burning, frequent urination, blood in the urine, or dark/foamy urine)?
During a flare, do you have costovertebral angle (back/side) tenderness or pain when pressing on the flank area?
During a flare, have you noticed blood in your urine at any time (even without burning/urgency), and if so what color is it (pink/red vs dark/tea-colored)?
During the flank-pain episodes, have you had any results from a urine test (urinalysis/culture), and did it show white blood cells and/or bacterial growth?
During a non-UTI flare, have you had a urinalysis and urine culture, and if so did they show blood or infection markers (e.g., leukocyte esterase/WBCs/nitrites or bacterial growth)?
During a flank-pain flare, do you have pain when you urinate (burning) or do you notice any urinary frequency/urgency even if you don’t feel “UTI-like”?
answers: Doctor: Did the flank pain start after a specific injury or fall, and if so, when did it occur? Patient: No, it didn’t start after any injury or fall—it’s been intermittent for about 5 months. I can’t link it to any specific event.
Patient: I don’t have any wrist pain or swelling—my issue is intermittent flank pain for about 5 months. I haven’t noticed redness or warmth in that area during flare-ups either.
Patient: No, I haven’t had fever, night sweats, or any unexplained weight loss.
Patient: No—I don’t have left wrist swelling, visible lumps, or any limited range of motion during episodes. My symptoms have been intermittent flank pain instead, without fever, nausea, or vomiting.

Patient: During the times I’m having urinary tract infections, I’ve had burning and some urgency, and I’ve occasionally noticed blood in my urine. But outside of those UTI episodes, my urinary habits are otherwise pretty normal—no dark or foamy urine, and no current fever.

Patient: Yes—when the flank pain flares, I do feel tenderness on the side/back area when it’s pressed, and the pain is localized there rather than in the abdomen. It comes and goes over time, and I don’t usually have nausea or vomiting with it.

Patient: Yes, during some of the episodes I’ve noticed blood in my urine—it's been more like pink to red rather than dark or tea-colored. I usually notice it along with the UTI-type symptoms, like burning and urgency. Outside of those infection times, I haven’t noticed blood.

Patient: I’ve had urine tests during those UTI episodes, and they’ve come back positive—showing signs of infection with white blood cells and bacterial growth. I don’t recall the exact numbers, but I was treated with antibiotics each time based on the results. Outside of those flare-ups, I haven’t had similar test results.

Patient: I haven’t had a urinalysis or urine culture done during the non-UTI flank-pain flares, so I don’t know if there were blood or infection markers then. When I did have UTIs, the tests were positive with WBCs and bacterial growth, and I was treated with antibiotics. Outside of those episodes, my urinary habits are otherwise pretty normal.

Patient: During the flare periods when I’ve had UTIs, I do get burning when I urinate and some urgency. Outside of those UTI episodes, I don’t usually notice increased frequency or urgency, and the flank tenderness still comes and goes.
